title: AI-enhanced electrocardiography for detection and prediction of dilated cardiomyopathy
summary: A deep learning ECG model trained on over 330,000 ECG-echocardiogram pairs detects the echocardiographic dilated cardiomyopathy phenotype (AUROC 0.87-0.97) and predicts incident disease with a C-index of 0.80-0.87, comparable to echocardiography. In two familial cohorts (Antwerp, Maastricht) 5-year negative predictive values were 95.5% and 91.5%, with positive predictive values of 42.4% and 39.4%. Authors describe the model as supporting exclusion of short- to mid-term disease, not as a diagnostic replacement.
ai_technology: Explainable deep learning model applied to 12-lead ECG
organization: Imperial College London; University of Antwerp and Antwerp University Hospital; Maastricht University Medical Center; Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center; UK Biobank cohorts; Zhongshan Hospital of Fudan University

evidence.tested: Validated in UK Biobank, Zhongshan Hospital and Antwerp cohorts, and in two familial cohorts (Antwerp n=166, Maastricht n=177), compared with traditional ECG features and echocardiographic traits.
evidence.unknown: Whether the model was locked and evaluated prospectively is not stated in the abstract; familial-cohort outcomes are reported as 5-year follow-up. Detailed limits not stated in the reviewed material.
evidence.ai_role: Deep learning model trained to detect and predict the echocardiographic DCM phenotype from ECG; explainable AI-ECG outperformed traditional ECG parameters.
